corrections.was: Node scale is a scale left on the node, instead of baked into the mesh. Here a ball is squashed by a node scale of one by zero point four, but its sphere collider has only one radius, so it sticks out zero point six metres above and below. A scale left on the node reaches everything built from the mesh. For example, a boulder flattened in Blender without applying scale keeps that scale on its node, and the player bumps into air above it.
corrections.now: Node scale is a scale left on the node, instead of baked into the mesh. Here a ball is squashed by a node scale of one by zero point four, but its sphere collider has only one radius, so it sticks out zero point six metres above and below. A scale left on the node reaches everything built from the mesh. For example, a boulder flattened in Blender without applying scale keeps that scale on its node, so a sphere collider leaves the player bumping into air above it.
corrections.why: A scale left on the node does not by itself make a collider stick out: Chapter 3 says anything generated from the mesh inherits the scale, so the bump into air needs a shape that cannot follow the stretch, the slide's sphere collider ('A sphere has one radius. It cannot follow a stretched mesh').
